item.title: Minnesota Vikings lose, saving the 1972 Miami Dolphins' 17-0 mark
item.description: The Miami Dolphins' season might not be going anywhere but a group of former players likely were enjoying champagne toasts Sunday. On the first day of November and with the season not even half over, the NFL's last unbeaten team fell. The Detroit Lions defeated the Minnesota Vikings 19-15 — meaning the 1972 Dolphins will remain the league's only undefeated champions. The surviving Dolphins from that perfect Super Bowl team have been celebrating every year once the NFL's last undefeated team loses. They usually have champagne and make a toast - and share that on social media. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs finished with 153 yards on 23 carries to lead the win over the Vikings . This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Minnesota Vikings lose, saving the 1972 Miami Dolphins' 17-0 mark

item.title: Dan Campbell Speaks About Jack Campbell Following Lions’ Win Over Vikings
item.description: The Detroit Lions picked up one of their biggest victories of the season Sunday afternoon, defeating the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings 19-15 at Ford Field. However, the celebration was understandably subdued following the frightening fourth-quarter injury to star linebacker Jack Campbell . Following the victory, head coach Dan Campbell addressed the situation and made it clear that his thoughts were with his injured defensive leader. Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell (46) warms up against the against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Dan Campbell Provides Update on Jack Campbell “Thoughts and prayers are with Jack and his family. He’s being taken care of. We don’t have any new information,” Dan Campbell said following Sunday’s victory. "We're thinking about him." Coach Campbell said the team does not have any new information on Jack Campbell's injury. pic.twitter.com/5huaEszj9O — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 1, 2026 The update came after Jack Campbell was transported to a local hospital for evaluation of a neck injury . The All-Pro linebacker was injured early in the fourth quarter while tackling former Lions tight end T.J. Hockenson. As we previously reported following the frightening injury , Campbell remained motionless on the turf for several minutes while medical personnel attended to him. He was eventually secured to a backboard and carted off the field as teammates gathered around him. Several Lions players were visibly emotional, and the defense gathered in prayer following the frightening incident . Although Dan Campbell confirmed that Jack was receiving medical care, he did not provide a diagnosis, prognosis, or timetable for his return. Lions Rally to Finish Off Previously Unbeaten Vikings Despite the emotional circumstances, Detroit managed to finish the game and hand Minnesota its first loss of the season. The Lions improved to 5-2, while the Vikings fell to 6-1. Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 153 yards, and Jared Goff connected with Jameson Williams for the decisive fourth-quarter touchdown. The victory was particularly impressive considering the injuries Detroit suffered throughout the afternoon. Earlier in the game, we reported that Brian Branch and DJ Wonnum were ruled out with concussions , leaving the Lions’ defense severely shorthanded. Still, Detroit found a way to close out a crucial divisional victory. But as Dan Campbell’s postgame comments demonstrated, the result was not the only thing on everyone’s mind. The Lions earned an important win Sunday. Now, they’re hoping for encouraging news about one of their most important players.

item.title: Why didn't the NFL flex the Eagles vs. Commanders game on SNF?
item.description: It is a day-after Halloween scary matchup — scary bad, not scary good — on "Sunday Night Football." The Philadelphia Eagles (2-5) face the Washington Commanders (1-4-1) in a battle of NFC East rivals, who with a combined three wins were hoping to have better records at this point in Week 8 of the NFL season. NFL: Former UTEP football star Tyrice Knight seizes starting NFL role for Seahawks The injury-plagued Eagles lost their last game, 38-21, to the Dallas Cowboys in Philadelphia. Washington lost their last game to the San Francisco 49ers, 17-23. The Commanders have only won one game this season (a 33-31 victory over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3) and tied with the New York Giants , 27-27, in Week 5. Philadelphia won its previous matchup with Washington 22-24 on Sept. 13 in Week 1 of the NFL season. What channel is Sunday Night Football on? The "Sunday Night Football" game between the Eagles and Commanders can be seen at 6:20 p.m. MT/ 7:20 p.m. CT on Sunday, Nov. 1, on NBC, and is also available streaming on Peacock. Where to watch Eagles vs Commanders Matchup: Eagles vs. Commanders Date: Nov. 1 Time: 6:20 p.m. MT/ 7:20 p.m. CT Venue: Northwest Stadium Location: Landover, Maryland TV: NBC, Peacock Why didn't the NFL flex the Eagles-Commanders game on SNF? The "Sunday Night Football" game on Nov. 1 features two teams with a combined three wins. Why didn't the NFL flex the game for a better matchup in Week 8? The NFL had a deadline of Oct. 20 to move a different matchup to occupy the prime-time slot on NBC for Week 8, but the league opted to keep things as-is, USA Today reported. The NFL's "flexible scheduling" rules began in 2006 to allow it to "to promote quality matchups" and has guidelines, deadlines and limits on when changes can be made. The guidelines per NFL.com via USA Today: Sunday Night Football: Can be flexed up to twice between Weeks 5-10, and any game during Weeks 11-17. The NFL must decide and notify all involved teams of the switch 12 days in advance for Weeks 5-13. After Week 13, the league only needs to notify teams six days in advance. Monday Night Football: Can be flexed any week between Weeks 12-17. As with its Sunday night counterpart, "MNF" flexes require 12 days of notice. Unlike its Sunday night counterpart, that window never shrinks to six days. Thursday Night Football: Can be flexed up to twice between Weeks 13-17. Those decisions must "be made no later than 21 days prior to the game." Daniel Borunda may be reached at dborunda@elpasotimes.com and @BorundaDaniel on X. USA Today contributed to this report. item.title: Bengals' Joe Burrow has his first 6-touchdown game vs Titans
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow threw five touchdown passes in a game for the third time in his NFL career during the team's NFL Week 8 game against the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium, and added a rushing TD in overtime to give him his first six-TD game in the league. Burrow had thrown five TD passes in a game twice, but didn't run for a TD in either game. Both of those games happened during the 2024 season. Four different receivers caught TD passes from Burrow against Tennessee. Tee Higgins caught a pair of Burrow TD passes. Earlier in the game, Burrow moved past Carson Palmer on the franchise's all-time passing-yardage list. Burrow entered the game needing 232 yards to move into fourth place among Bengals' QBs in passing yards. Only Ken Anderson (32,838), Andy Dalton (31,594) and Boomer Esiason (27,149) have more passing yards with the franchise than Burrow. item.title: Syracuse football: takeaways from the win over SMU
item.description: SYRACUSE, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 31: The Syracuse Orange celebrate following a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the SMU Mustangs at JMA Wireless Dome on October 31, 2026 in Syracuse, New York. (Photo by Rebecca Villagracia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Two weeks ago, it seemed like everyone was wondering how much longer it would take Syracuse to pick up another conference win. Following yet another ACC loss at the hands of Virginia, coupled with more injuries at the quarterback position, it was difficult to see when, or even how, the Orange would finally get back on track. But seemingly out of nowhere everything changed. Syracuse went on the road and stunned North Carolina in overtime before returning home and knocking off a ranked SMU squad in front of its own fans. Just like that, the Orange have put together back-to-back conference victories, and suddenly, there is a lot more optimism surrounding this team. Here are the biggest takeaways from Syracuse’s win over the SMU yesterday: Fran Brown has established the run game With Steve Angeli back under center and looking healthy, opposing defenses have to be much more conscious of what Syracuse can accomplish through the air. That added threat in the passing game has also opened up opportunities for the Orange to establish a more consistent ground attack. Between Ahmad Miller and Tylik Hill, Syracuse combined for 28 carries and 110 rushing yards, providing a solid foundation for the offense as a whole. A very respectable day on the ground, which is something the Orange have really struggled with in the past. It’s also worth noting that Syracuse has found success with a two-headed monster in the backfield rather than relying on one running back to shoulder the bulk of the workload. With both Miller and Hill receiving a healthy share of the carries, the Orange can spread out the responsibilities while keeping both backs involved. It also gives Fran Brown more flexibility when making personnel decisions and allows him to get creative with how he utilizes each running back in the offense. Calvin Russell makes an impact The five-star freshman has arrived, and early signs suggest he could be the real deal. At first glance, his stat line may not jump off the page, with just three receptions for 41 yards. However, the box score doesn’t tell the whole story when it comes to the impact he made against SMU. Between the touchdown reception in the back of the end zone that was ultimately overturned and a lengthy screen pass that was negated by a holding penalty, there were several flashes of what makes him such an exciting young talent. The production may not have shown up in the final numbers, but the playmaking ability was certainly on display. Moving forward, No. 5 is someone defenses are going to need to keep a close eye on whenever he steps onto the field, and will continue to open up opportunities for Umari Hatcher who continues to ball out week after week. item.title: Teenage Coventry fan hands himself in to police after taunting Sunderland supporters with image of Bradley Lowery
item.description: Sunderland v Preston North End - Sky Bet Championship - Getty Images Sport A 14-year-old Coventry City fan has handed himself in to police after using a photograph of the late Bradley Lowery to taunt Sunderland supporters during Saturday's Premier League clash at the Coventry Building Society Arena. Bradley's mother, Gemma Lowery, has called the act heartbreaking but urged people not to direct hate at the boy, who is the same age her son would be now. Coventry fan taunts Sunderland supporters with Lowery photograph According to talkSPORT , a video of the incident during Coventry's 3-1 win over Sunderland at the Coventry Building Society Arena went viral on social media. The clip showed the teenager taunting fans in the away end by pointing to an image of Lowery on his phone. Lowery, a young Sunderland supporter, died from stage four neuroblastoma, a rare and aggressive form of cancer, in 2017 at the age of six . He became the club's mascot and formed a close bond with then-Black Cats striker Jermain Defoe, while his family raised £1.3 million for treatment only available in the USA. West Midlands Police confirm 14-year-old has handed himself in Coventry were quick to respond after learning of the footage, releasing a statement that read: "Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland. The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action." West Midlands Police have since confirmed that the boy has handed himself in. "We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City's Premier League match with Sunderland yesterday afternoon (31 Oct)," their statement read. "A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course. We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim's family and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs." Gemma Lowery says mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter Gemma, who helped launch the Bradley Lowery Foundation in August 2017 to support families fundraising for treatment or equipment not covered by the NHS, responded on the foundation's page. "My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate," she wrote. "Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. item.title: Buccaneers make NFL history, first team since 1974 to win without completing a pass
item.description: At the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' victory celebration following their 16-0 victory over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, they are going to party like it's 1974. The Buccaneers became the first team since the 1974 Buffalo Bills and the third team ever to win while completing zero passes. Quarterback Baker Mayfield attempted just three passes (to three different receivers) and didn't complete any. Mayfield nearly completed a deep pass to Ted Hurst , but the rookie wide receiver couldn't hang on to the pass that would have brought the Bucs inside the five-yard line. A torrential downpour that lasted from kickoff until the final whistle marred the playing conditions at Raymond James Stadium, the Bucs' home. Puddles soaked midfield. Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. struggled mightily, with eight completions on 24 attempts for 125 yards – and four interceptions. Mayfield (39.6) had a higher passer rating than Penix (0.0). Tampa Bay had little trouble running the ball, however. Running backs Bucky Irving (170 yards) and Kenneth Gainwell (110 yards) combined for 310 rushing yards, while Mayfield contributed 14 on four attempts. Irving scored the game's lone touchdown (a four-yard run), while Tampa Bay controlled the ball for 35:16. Atlanta was 0-for-12 on third downs. item.title: Union Berlin gift quiz-show contestant “Spassikowski” shirt after amusing blunder
item.description: Union Berlin gift quiz-show contestant “Spassikowski” shirt after amusing blunder One of the Bundesliga’s more amusing recent stories has acquired a rather fitting sequel. After failing to identify Union Berlin head coach Mauro Lustrinelli on Germany’s popular quiz show Wer wird Millionär? ( Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? ), unfortunate contestant Noah Petrik has the Köpenick club up on their invitation. And Union have ensured that the 26-year-old will never forget the name he mistakenly selected. Petrik was invited to Sunday’s Bundesliga home fixture against 1. FC Cologne and presented with a personalised Union Berlin shirt bearing the name “Spassikowski”. This was one of four possible answers to a €2,000 quiz-show question asking Petrik, an Augsburg native, to identify Union’s current head coach. And, unfortunately for the contestant, it was the wrong one. A new Bundesliga keepsake for Petrik Petrik encountered the question during an appearance on the RTL programme hosted by Günther Jauch. The four possible answers were Igor Spassikowski, Mauro Lustrinelli, Erling Gaudigaard, and Jimmy Sexyhexi. Unable to identify the correct name, Petrik utilized his “phone-a-friend” option. Petrik’s friend, despite professing to be a football fan, admitted that his knowledge might be a little outdated. The friend nevertheless confidently suggested Igor Spassikowski. Petrik trusted him. The result was a €1,500 mistake, with the contestant leaving the programme with just €500. Union’s social-media department wasted little time joining the fun, posting the question alongside a photograph of the real Lustrinelli and suggesting that the correct answer was actually D: Jimmy Sexyhexi. The Swiss trainer also enjoyed the incident and extended an invitation to Petrik to attend a match. “I think it’s funny, including the suggested names,” Lustrinelli explained at the time in comments reported by Sport Bild . “There are some nice ideas among them. That’s why I’d like to warmly invite the contestant to watch one of our matches and get to know us a little better.” Union ensure Spassikowski lives on The club duly followed through on that invitation ahead of Sunday’s encounter with Cologne at the Stadion An der Alten Försterei. Petrik received a Union shirt emblazoned with the name that had cost him his chance to continue playing for a substantial cash prize. One imagines the jersey will serve as a particularly effective reminder should he ever encounter another Bundesliga coaching question. Still, for Petrik, the visit provided a rather enjoyable consolation prize. He may not have left Günther Jauch’s television studio with €2,000, but he now owns what must surely be one of the most unusual personalised Bundesliga shirts in circulation. And if anyone asks him who coaches Union Berlin these days, at least he has a pretty good conversation starter. GGFN | Peter Weis

item.title: Tributes to 'inspirational' Olympian Ciara Mageean after death at 34
item.description: A statement posted on Mageean's social media on Sunday said she died surrounded by her loved ones [Getty Images] Tributes have been paid to former European champion and two-time Olympic runner Ciara Mageean, who has died at the age of 34. Mageean, from Portaferry in County Down, was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025. She died on Sunday morning, surrounded by her loved ones, a statement posted on her social media accounts said. "A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed," it said. Mageean's death comes less than three weeks after her marriage to her long-term partner Thomas Moran . The athlete represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics and won gold in the 1500m at the European Athletics Championships in Rome in 2024. She also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning silver in Birmingham in 2022. 'One of our own' Olympic legend Lady Mary Peters said Mageean was a "wonderful lady" who was "gracious, beautiful, talented and inspirational to the next generation". "We knew she was very ill and we knew that it was inevitable but we didn't expect it so soon," said the 1972 Olympic pentathlon gold medallist. Lady Mary's charity the Mary Peters Trust, which supports Northern Ireland athletes, had helped Mageean in her athletics career. "My charity supported her for as long as we could because she was so talented and we recognised that in her," said Last Mary. She said that Mageean had continued to inspire young athletes even while undergoing treatment for cancer and would be "sorely missed in the world of sport". item.title: Big 12 admits replay officials were ‘incorrect’ overturning BYU-ASU fumble call
item.description: Credit: Fox Sports Another week, another brutal mistake by Big 12 officials. The No. 8 BYU Cougars held off the Arizona State Sun Devils on Saturday for a 27-20 win, but the winning score came courtesy of what the conference later admitted was an incorrect call by its replay officials. With the score 0-0, BYU had the ball on 2nd-and-goal in the first quarter when quarterback Bear Bachmeier fumbled on a sneak attempt. Running back Sione Moa eventually picked it up and rolled into the end zone. Field officials initially ruled that Bachmeier’s forward progress had stopped, ending the play. However, the Big 12’s replay review officials reviewed the play and overturned the call, crediting BYU with a touchdown. At the time, the decision stymied the Fox announcing booth, including rules analyst Mike Pereira, who has clearly gotten sick of calling out bad Big 12 official decisions . “This is not the type of situation that you have when a runner steps out of bounds where you can continue in action,” Pereira said on the broadcast. “This was a player that recovered the ball and got up in the field of play. The ruling on the field was the runner was down initially. And if that’s the case, you’ve ruled it dead. You can give a recovery, but you can’t give an advance, unless you’ve come up with a new rule here, which I’m not too sure you can really do.” “This is getting kind of frustrating, you know, week to week,” he continued. “You know, we shouldn’t have these situations that we come up, and then we have further explanation as the week wears on… They killed the play. You can forget about when the whistle happened. They killed the play in the field of play, and the ball was out. Give the recovery, but not the advance.” After the game, the Big 12 issued a statement admitting that the replay officials made an “incorrect” call and that a touchdown should not have been awarded. At 11:27 in the first period of the Arizona State-BYU game, Big 12 Replay Officials stopped the game to review possession by BYU. The play showed that the runner lost possession of the ball prior to the forward progress spot, and the ball was recovered by another BYU player at the two-yard line and he was awarded a touchdown. Rule 12-3-3-d-2 states, “If the replay official rules that the ball was not dead, it belongs to the recovering team at the spot of the recovery and any advance is nullified.” Replay was incorrect in awarding a score. The correct ruling should have been BYU ball for a third and goal attempt from the two-yard line. item.title: Star confirms it: He remains on course to leave Liverpool
item.description: Star confirms it: He remains on course to leave Liverpool One Liverpool star has completely confirmed it. He remains on course to leave the Reds and his situation is yet to change. 2026 was a year of goodbyes at Liverpool as they saw some key players depart the club. Three of them were planned, though not all of them. Mohamed Salah was the biggest departure. He left along with Andy Robertson at the end of the season, with Liverpool allowing both to leave on free transfers. Ibrahima Konate then did the same - even if the Reds did try to keep him around. Curtis Jones then called time on his Liverpool career. He agreed to join Inter in the summer as he'd entered the final year of his contract. The club were willing to sell before losing him for nothing next year. And similar situations will pop up again. Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker are the headliners this time around and both are set to leave with the end of their respective contracts in 2027. But they're not the only difficult situations. Alexis Mac Allister's contract situation Liverpool controversially decided not to renew Alexis Mac Allister 's contract this year, despite handing major deals to both Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai. The trio have made up their midfield since 2023, arriving at the same time. But the Reds made their choice here. They opted against Mac Allister, who has a deal until 2028, and that's something that upset the player. We know that because the Argentine went public with his disappointment - he wants to renew and it's Liverpool who aren't playing ball. Things have changed, though. In as much as Mac Allister has started the season brilliantly and is clearly Liverpool's best midfielder right now. He's become absolutely vital to Andoni Iraola and it's thought that some pressure there could change the situation and secure him a new contract. However, it hasn't had an effect thus far. Mac Allister gave an interview to Sky Sports this week where he made it clear that the situation hasn't changed. He remains on course to leave in 2028, though expectations are that Liverpool would look to sell early next year in order to receive some sort of fee with which to sign a replacement. The season is still young, of course, but as things stand, this increasingly looks like the final season of Mac Allister at Liverpool.

item.description: In what felt like a replay of Week 1’s loss , the Cleveland Browns were blown out by the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season. A matchup of the top two teams in the AFC North, the Steelers controlled the game from start to finish, with Cleveland struggling on both sides of the ball . While not a major impact on the game, and both returned to the contest, a few injuries on the defense didn’t help the Browns’ cause . A few key takeaways, few positive, from the train wreck that was Week 8 for Cleveland: Young teams are inconsistent Not an excuse, but important to note that the Browns are a very young team facing a veteran-laden Steelers squad for the second time this year. Cleveland was also on the road in a very tough place to play. Deshaun Watson’s early struggles with quick decisions Simply put, quarterback play in the NFL is all about going through the first two reads while in your drop back and throwing the ball when you hit your back foot. Even at his best, that has not been Watson’s game, which leads to more sacks and what looks like “running for your life” plays. Those plays will happen, at times, throughout the league, but most quarterbacks are throwing passes as players are in their break or before; Watson is often waiting until they are out of their breaks. Was this game all on the quarterback? Not at all; problems were all over the place. Just notable that it seems like Watson isn’t getting protection, but his style of play doesn’t help either. Ronnie Hickman’s poor angle leads to 2 big gains 51 on third and long and 23 yards late in the 2nd quarter to get Pittsburgh near midfield, leading to a late first-half touchdown were both because Cleveland’s safety took horrible angles in run support. Trying anything for a kick return spark Nothing really popped, but interesting that Isaiah Bond took the first kickoff, then it was Malachi Corley , followed by Dylan Sampson . item.title: From Fleetwood embarrassment to 'magical' Anfield win 14 years in making
item.description: "Today has to be the day." That is what manager Mikel Arteta said before Arsenal secured their first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years, beating Liverpool thanks to Kai Havertz's first-half goal . Arteta was Arsenal captain the last time the Gunners won at Liverpool - 2-0 in 2012 - and they have had 16 unsuccessful trips in all competitions until Sunday's victory. The Spaniard's side, as they so often do, produced a defensive masterclass to keep out wave after wave of Liverpool attack to deliver a rare and historic win. Arsenal travelled to Anfield after an embarrassing loss to League Two Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday. Arteta said he thought that humbling loss in Lancashire could spur his side on to a historic win at Liverpool. "Extremely proud. It's been 14 years, that's a long time," Arteta said after the game. "I'm sure we made everybody attached to the club extremely proud today. Not only for the victory but for the way we've done it, the spirit we've shown. "Especially considering what happened four days ago when you lose and go out of the cup against a team you are supposed to beat. That's the magical part of this game, it can take you to really bad places but four days later you have the opportunity to do something really historic and we've done it. "Overall, to win against a team that is producing what they are doing, and also in the emotional state after Fleetwood, that's what a winning team should do." Before the match, centre-back Gabriel said that Arsenal were expecting a "big battle" and "big chaos" against Liverpool. That prediction was correct and, after going ahead, Arsenal were pinned back before the break. Although the second half was a bit calmer, they still defended resolutely and did not allow Liverpool a shot on target. The Gunners, who have kept six clean sheets this season, are now three points clear at the top of the table after nine games. I'll tell my players to dive in future - Iraola Arsenal have kept six clean sheets in the Premier League this season [Getty Images] 'The togetherness we have is undefeated' Arsenal's 24 points is the most by any team after nine games of a season since the Gunners themselves in 2022-23.
